title: attn-prefetch-scheduler-and-rotary-offset-squeeze
author: Jordan Kim
description:
Context: production workloads with mixed sequence distributions (chat plus long-context retrieval) expose two friction points: 1) inefficient prefetch and reservation of KV cache leading to intermittent tail latency spikes when new contexts miss the fastpath, and 2) overhead from rotary/rope coordinate recomputation across fused attention paths. This PR introduces a coordinated change to the attention runtime: a two-tier prefetch scheduler and a lightweight rotary-offset-squeeze transform that reduces per-token rotary arithmetic when possible. The changes are designed to be backward-compatible with existing model configs and to be toggled via config flags for staged rollout.

What this PR does (high level): implement a prefetch scheduler that maintains priority lanes (latency-sensitive, throughput, and background fill) and an adaptive reservation window for KV cache; introduce a rotary-offset-squeeze transform operator that detects contiguous rotary offsets and emits a compact representation for the fastpath fused-attention kernels; add kernel hooks so the runtime can switch between 'squeezed-rotary' and standard rotary at the model-layer granularity.

Technical details: the prefetch scheduler runs in the request router before request batching and performs lightweight sequence-length prediction and cache-residency estimation; based on policy it either: a) place request in low-latency lane and pre-allocate a small KV reservation, b) schedule into batcher with optimistic prefetch, or c) mark as background for rehydrate-only scenarios. Reservation bookkeeping uses an LRU-informed window and exposes metrics for predicted vs actual hit rates. The rotary-offset-squeeze transform identifies when rotary index offsets increase monotonically within a tile and encodes the base offset plus stride, enabling the fused-attn kernel to apply a single vectorized rotary instead of repeated scalar ops.

Compatibility and rollout: default behavior is unchanged. New behavior is gated by two server-side config flags: runtime.attn.prefetch_enabled and runtime.attn.rotary_squeeze_enabled. The PR includes config migration docs and a canary rollout plan: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with metrics monitored (p95 latency, KV hit rate delta, token/sec).

Benchmarks: measured on p4d-like machines with mixes representative of product workloads (50% chat seq<=128, 35% seq 256-512, 15% long seq 1024+). Observed median improvements after enabling both features: throughput +1.18x at seq512 under sustained load; p95 latency reduced by 17% for latency lane requests at small batch sizes (<=4); average GPU memory overhead for KV reservations reduced by ~9% due to tighter reservation windows; rotary arithmetic reduced by ~22% in fused-kernel fastpath, measured as FLOP-equivalent reduction. Microbenchmarks: fused-attn kernel with squeezed rotary shows a 9-14% speedup depending on head count and dtype (fp16/tf32).

Tests and CI: unit tests for scheduler state machine and rotary encoder edge cases; integration tests that run a synthetic workload harness against the local runtime with and without the flags; perf CI job included a 30-min soak run on perf-lab cluster (initial run flaky due to a race in reservation bookkeeping; fixed in second commit). All CI checks passed on merge.

Files of note changed: runtime/attn/prefetch_scheduler.py, runtime/attn/rotary_squeeze.cu, runtime/attn/kv_reservation.cc, runtime/attn/kernel_hooks.h, tests/attn/test_prefetch_scheduler.py, benchmarks/attn/prefetch_soak.yaml, docs/ops/rotary_squeeze.md.

Follow-ups: 1) extend reservation estimator with per-customer heuristics (ENG-4187), 2) add telemetry-derived automated lane assignment to replace simple heuristics, 3) explore further fusion opportunities combining KV eviction hints with rotary squeeze encoding.

Summary: this change reduces tail latency variance and CPU/GPU cost in mixed workloads with a conservative, feature-flagged rollout and clear telemetry.

review_comments: Aisha Patel: Please add a short blurb in the runtime docs about how rotary_squeeze interacts with model quantization — I want to avoid surprises when models switch to int8.
Jordan Kim: Added docs/ops/rotary_squeeze.md and a note about quantization; the kernel emits a fallback scalar path for int8 where the squeeze is not safe.
Carlos Mendez: Nice work — can you clarify how reservation window growth behaves under bursty traffic? I want to ensure we don't over-allocate on transient spikes.
Jordan Kim: Reservation window uses exponential backoff with a max cap and decays after stable low-miss periods; added unit tests for burst scenario.
Linnea Berg: Perf numbers look promising; please include a canary plan and alert thresholds in release notes.
Jordan Kim: Canary plan added to description and release notes; alerts wired to p95 > baseline*1.15 and KV miss delta > 5%
release_notes: Introduce prefetch scheduler with priority lanes and rotary-offset-squeeze transform. Performance improvements for mixed-length workloads: ~1.18x throughput at seq512 and reduced p95 latency for latency-sensitive requests. Flagged rollout: runtime.attn.prefetch_enabled=false, runtime.attn.rotary_squeeze_enabled=false by default. See docs/ops/rotary_squeeze.md for details and quantization considerations.
